docs.text: HardFOC core library Functional Pin Configuration ¶ One header per HardFOC board that says what every pin does, which chip carries it and how it is driven. The GPIO and ADC layers of a board HAL register their pins from it, so a pin number is written exactly once. Quickstart Vortex V1 pins Flux V1 pins A pin map copied into managers, examples and documents drifts: the schematic changes, one copy is updated and the board misbehaves in a way no compiler catches. hf-pincfg keeps each board's map as X-macro rows in one header. Expanding the rows produces the functional enums, the name and category tables and the constexpr mapping arrays that the board HAL iterates. The tables on this site are generated from the same rows. What you get ¶ Functional names, not GPIO numbers. Code asks for HfFunctionalGpioPin::SPI2_CS_TMC9660 ; the row says it is MCU GPIO 18, active low, pulled up. See Pin model . Pins on any chip. A row can live on the MCU, an I/O expander (PCAL95555) or a motor controller's GPIO (TMC9660), so expander pins are first-class. See the Vortex V1 pin map . Electrical settings with the pin. Polarity, pull, drive mode and maximum current travel in the same row. ADC channels with their scaling. Resolution, full-scale voltage and divider ratio per channel. See the API guide . Compile-time board selection. One HARDFOC_BOARD_* define picks the header; no runtime tables, no heap. See Integration . Header-only C++20. Nothing to link; the arrays are constexpr . Used by ¶ Repository How hf-hal-vortex-v1 Defines HARDFOC_BOARD_VORTEX_V1 ; GpioManager registers every GPIO-category row hf-hal-flux-v1 Flux V1 board HAL; selects HARDFOC_BOARD_FLUX_V1 hf-core Adds src/ to the include path; host builds define HARDFOC_BOARD_NONE hf-core-drivers Carries this repository as the internal/hf-pincfg submodule Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Select a board and walk its pin map in a dozen lines. Pin model One X-macro row, every field explained. Vortex V1 pin map ESP32-C6, PCAL95555 and TMC9660 pins, generated from the header. Flux V1 pin map ESP32-S3 pins for the MAX22200, TLE92466ED and ADS7952. Adding a board Write a new header and hook it into the selector.

docs.text: Adding a board ¶ Write a board header, hook it into the selector and generate its pin table, in five steps. Copy the closest board header. Start from src/hf_functional_pin_config_vortex_v1.hpp or src/hf_functional_pin_config_flux_v1.hpp and name it hf_functional_pin_config_<board>.hpp , with its own include guard. Define the chips. Edit HfGpioChipType and HfAdcChipType so they list the chips that carry pins on this board, MCU first ( = 0 ). Write the rows. One X(...) per pin in HF_FUNCTIONAL_GPIO_PIN_LIST and per channel in HF_FUNCTIONAL_ADC_CHANNEL_LIST , grouped by category, with the fields from the pin model . Take every number from the schematic; record wiring facts in a /* ... */ comment above the row. Keep the generated-table section and the helper functions unchanged. Hook it into the selector. Add an #elif defined(HARDFOC_BOARD_<BOARD>) branch to src/hf_functional_pin_config.hpp and the macro to the #error message. Document it. Add the board to BOARDS in tools/docs/generators/pins.py , copy docs/vortex-v1.md to a page for the board with its region names ( pins-<board> , adc-<board> ), add the page to docs/.nav.yml and run hardfoc-docs gen . Check it ¶ c++ -std = c++20 -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -Isrc -DHARDFOC_BOARD_<BOARD> tests/docs/quickstart.cpp hardfoc-docs gen --check mkdocs build --strict The first line compiles every documented call against the new map. Then bump the submodule in the board HAL and define the macro there. Rules for rows ¶ Rule Why Rows never move between categories silently The HAL's GPIO manager registers gpio and user rows only Chip selects and resets are PIN_LOGIC_INVERTED when the net is active low Drivers set logical levels; the row holds the polarity A net reachable from two chips gets two rows, one per chip, with a comment Vortex V1 TMC9660 GPIO17/18 are the example No pin number outside the header Examples that call the SDK directly read it from the map or a constant derived from it Next: Testing and CI .
docs.title: Adding a board

docs.text: API guide ¶ Look up pins and channels, filter them and turn ADC counts into volts, by task. Every block compiles against both boards. The shape of the API ¶ Task Call Returns One pin's row GetGpioMapping(HfFunctionalGpioPin) const HfGpioMapping* , nullptr if out of range One ADC channel's row GetAdcMapping(HfFunctionalAdcChannel) const HfAdcMapping* or nullptr Every row HF_GPIO_MAPPING[] , HF_ADC_MAPPING[] with ..._SIZE constexpr arrays Name of a pin or channel to_string(pin) , to_string(channel) std::string_view , "UNKNOWN_PIN" if out of range Owner of a pin get_pin_category(pin) , should_register_as_gpio(category) HfPinCategory , bool Pins by owner or chip GetGpioPinsByCategory() , GetGpioPinsByChipType() count written to your array Pull resistors RequiresPullUp(pin) , RequiresPullDown(pin) bool Availability IsGpioPinAvailable(pin) , IsAdcChannelAvailable(ch) bool Walk the pins a GPIO layer owns ¶ #include "hf_functional_pin_config.hpp" // the build defines one HARDFOC_BOARD_* macro // Print where every pin that the GPIO layer should own lives on this board. void list_gpio_pins () { for ( size_t i = 0 ; i < HF_GPIO_MAPPING_SIZE ; ++ i ) { const HfGpioMapping & m = HF_GPIO_MAPPING [ i ]; if ( ! should_register_as_gpio ( static_cast < HfPinCategory > ( m . category ))) { continue ; // core and comm pins belong to the system and the bus drivers } std :: printf ( "%-28.*s chip %u pin %2u %s \n " , static_cast < int > ( m . name . size ()), m . name . data (), m . chip_type , m . physical_pin , m . is_inverted ? "active-low" : "active-high" ); } } A board HAL does the same loop and creates a driver for each row on the chip chip_type names ( static_cast<HfGpioChipType>(m.chip_type) ). Look up one pin ¶ // Find one pin by function: the only place a pin number comes from. bool chip_select_is_active_low ( HfFunctionalGpioPin pin ) { const HfGpioMapping * m = GetGpioMapping ( pin ); if ( m == nullptr ) { return false ; // not on this board } return m -> is_inverted ; } The enum value indexes the arrays directly, so the lookup is a bounds check and an array access. Filter by chip ¶ // Every pin a given chip carries, without a heap. size_t pins_on_mcu ( HfFunctionalGpioPin ( & out )[ HF_GPIO_MAPPING_SIZE ]) { return GetGpioPinsByChipType ( HfGpioChipType :: ESP32_INTERNAL , out , HF_GPIO_MAPPING_SIZE ); } GetGpioPinsByCategory() works the same way with an HfPinCategory . Both write at most max_count entries and return how many they wrote. ADC channels ¶ // ADC channels carry their scaling: full-scale voltage, resolution and divider. float counts_to_volts ( HfFunctionalAdcChannel ch , uint32_t counts ) { const HfAdcMapping * m = GetAdcMapping ( ch ); if ( m == nullptr ) { return 0.0F ; } const float full_scale = static_cast < float > (( 1U << m -> resolution_bits ) - 1U ); return static_cast < float > ( counts ) / full_scale * ( static_cast < float > ( m -> max_voltage_mv ) / 1000.0F ) * m -> voltage_divider ; } max_voltage_mv is the full-scale input of the converter and voltage_divider the ratio of the external divider in front of it (Flux V1 bus voltage: 11.0 ). Names and categories ¶ // Names for logs and consoles; categories decide who owns a pin. void describe ( HfFunctionalGpioPin pin ) { const std :: string_view name = to_string ( pin ); const bool owned_by_gpio = should_register_as_gpio ( get_pin_category ( pin )); std :: printf ( "%.*s: %s \n " , static_cast < int > ( name . size ()), name . data (), owned_by_gpio ? "GPIO" : "reserved" ); } Board-specific constants ¶ A board header may export derived constants for code that calls the MCU SDK directly. Flux V1 has kFluxHwUartFdo2TxGpio and kFluxHwUartFdo2RxGpio , read from the UART_FDO2_TX / UART_FDO2_RX rows, so they cannot disagree with the map. Next: Adding a board .

docs.text: Pin model ¶ How one X-macro row describes a pin, what the rows expand into and who reads the result. One row per pin, every table generated Figure description and sources From top to bottom. The HAL's build defines one HARDFOC_BOARD_* macro; the selector header (src/hf_functional_pin_config.hpp) includes that board's header. The board header holds two X-macro lists, one row per GPIO function and one per ADC channel. Expanding the lists produces the enums, name and category tables and the mapping arrays (names read from the Vortex V1 header). The board HAL's managers iterate the mapping arrays and look pins up by enum; no other code writes a pin number. Drawn from: src/hf_functional_pin_config.hpp board selector ; src/hf_functional_pin_config_vortex_v1.hpp X-macro lists and generated tables ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/pin-model.py . One row per function ¶ Each board header defines two lists. HF_FUNCTIONAL_GPIO_PIN_LIST(X) has one X(...) row per digital pin; HF_FUNCTIONAL_ADC_CHANNEL_LIST(X) one row per analog channel. This row from the Vortex V1 header is the TMC9660 chip select: X ( SPI2_CS_TMC9660 , "COMM_SPI2_CS_TMC9660" , HfPinCategory :: PIN_CATEGORY_COMM , HfGpioChipType :: ESP32_INTERNAL , 0 , 0 , 18 , PIN_LOGIC_INVERTED , PIN_HAS_PULL , PIN_PULL_UP , PIN_PUSH_PULL , 40 ) Position Field In the example Meaning 1 ENUM_NAME SPI2_CS_TMC9660 Becomes HfFunctionalGpioPin::SPI2_CS_TMC9660 2 STRING_NAME "COMM_SPI2_CS_TMC9660" Name for logs and consoles; the prefix repeats the category 3 CATEGORY PIN_CATEGORY_COMM Who owns the pin (below) 4 CHIP_TYPE ESP32_INTERNAL Chip that carries the pin; each board header defines its own HfGpioChipType 5 CHIP_UNIT 0 Which instance of that chip (0 = first) 6 GPIO_BANK 0 Port or bank within the chip (0 = A) 7 PHYSICAL_PIN 18 Pin number within the bank: GPIO number on an ESP32, port bit 0 to 15 on a PCAL95555 8 LOGIC_INVERSION PIN_LOGIC_INVERTED Active low 9 HAS_PULL PIN_HAS_PULL A pull resistor is enabled 10 PULL_DIRECTION PIN_PULL_UP Up or down; ignored without a pull 11 OUTPUT_MODE PIN_PUSH_PULL Push-pull or open-drain 12 MAX_CURRENT_MA 40 Maximum current (mA) An ADC row has ten fields: enum and string name, chip type, chip unit, ADC unit, physical channel, resolution (bits), full-scale voltage (mV), divider ratio ( 1.0f = none) and a description. Categories ¶ Category Prefix Owned by should_register_as_gpio() PIN_CATEGORY_CORE CORE_ The MCU itself: crystal, strapping, USB false PIN_CATEGORY_COMM COMM_ A bus driver: SPI, UART, I²C, TWAI, LED data false PIN_CATEGORY_GPIO GPIO_ The HAL's GPIO manager true PIN_CATEGORY_USER Application-defined pins true is_reserved_prefix() tells whether a name starts with CORE_ , COMM_ , SYS_ or INTERNAL_ . What the rows expand into ¶ Every board header expands its lists with the same #define X(...) / #undef X pattern: Generated Type Index HfFunctionalGpioPin enum class : uint8_t , ends with HF_FUNCTIONAL_GPIO_COUNT row order HfFunctionalGpioPinNames[] std::string_view enum value HfFunctionalGpioPinCategories[] HfPinCategory enum value HF_GPIO_MAPPING[] , HF_GPIO_MAPPING_SIZE HfGpioMapping enum value HfFunctionalAdcChannel enum class : uint8_t , ends with HF_FUNCTIONAL_ADC_COUNT row order HfFunctionalAdcChannelNames[] std::string_view enum value HF_ADC_MAPPING[] , HF_ADC_MAPPING_SIZE HfAdcMapping enum value Because the enum and the arrays come from the same rows, HF_GPIO_MAPPING[static_cast<size_t>(pin)] is always the row of pin . The structures HfGpioMapping and HfAdcMapping and the category enum are shared by every board in src/hf_functional_pin_config_base.hpp . Board selection ¶ src/hf_functional_pin_config.hpp includes one board header: Define Board MCU Header GPIO rows ADC rows HARDFOC_BOARD_FLUX_V1 Flux V1 ESP32-S3 src/hf_functional_pin_config_flux_v1.hpp 27 14 HARDFOC_BOARD_VORTEX_V1 Vortex V1 ESP32-C6 src/hf_functional_pin_config_vortex_v1.hpp 34 15 HARDFOC_BOARD_NONE None (host builds) none src/hf_functional_pin_config_none.hpp 0 0 HARDFOC_BOARD_NONE (or HF_MCU_FAMILY_NONE ) selects an empty map for host builds: the enums have only their _COUNT entry and every lookup returns nullptr . The repository also has src/hf_functional_pin_config_pw_controller_v1.hpp , an STM32H747 carrier profile that the selector does not include yet. Design choices ¶ Primitive types only. Board headers use uint8_t , bool and their own enums, so the library depends on no MCU SDK and no driver. The HAL casts chip_type back to its board's HfGpioChipType . The header is the board's schematic in code. Comments in the rows record wiring facts (for example, that TMC9660 GPIO17 and GPIO18 are also wired to PCAL95555 inputs P1 and P2). No runtime registration code here. The library only describes; the HAL decides how to create drivers. Next: API guide .

docs.text: Primitive types only. Board headers use uint8_t , bool and their own enums, so the library depends on no MCU SDK and no driver. The HAL casts chip_type back to its board's HfGpioChipType . The header is the board's schematic in code. Comments in the rows record wiring facts (for example, that TMC9660 GPIO17 and GPIO18 are also wired to PCAL95555 inputs P1 and P2). No runtime registration code here. The library only describes; the HAL decides how to create drivers. Next: API guide .

docs.text: Integration ¶ Add the headers to a build, select the board and pick up the version, with plain CMake or ESP-IDF. Requirements ¶ Item Requirement Language C++20 ( std::string_view::starts_with ) Dependencies None: <cstdint> and <string_view> Files Header-only; everything is in src/ Heap, RTOS, exceptions None CMake ¶ The repository has no CMakeLists.txt : add src/ to the include path of the target that owns the board, and define the board there with PUBLIC scope so every consumer sees the same map. target_include_directories ( my_hal PUBLIC ${ CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR } /external/hf-pincfg/src ) target_compile_definitions ( my_hal PUBLIC HARDFOC_BOARD_FLUX_V1=1 ) hf-core does this for you: cmake/hf_core_build_settings.cmake adds hf-core-drivers/internal/hf-pincfg/src to its include directories, and a host build ( HF_CORE_MCU=NONE ) defines HARDFOC_BOARD_NONE . The board HAL then adds its own HARDFOC_BOARD_* define. ESP-IDF ¶ Inside an ESP-IDF component, add the folder to INCLUDE_DIRS and the define to the component's compile options: idf_component_register ( SRCS "my_hal.cpp" INCLUDE_DIRS "." "external/hf-pincfg/src" ) target_compile_definitions ( ${ COMPONENT_LIB } PUBLIC HARDFOC_BOARD_VORTEX_V1=1 ) target_compile_features ( ${ COMPONENT_LIB } PUBLIC cxx_std_20 ) Configuration macros ¶ Macro Set by Effect HARDFOC_BOARD_VORTEX_V1 Vortex V1 HAL Includes the Vortex V1 map HARDFOC_BOARD_FLUX_V1 Flux V1 HAL Includes the Flux V1 map HARDFOC_BOARD_NONE or HF_MCU_FAMILY_NONE Host builds Empty map, lookups return nullptr Exactly one must be defined. When several are, the first in the selector wins (Flux V1, then Vortex V1, then none); do not rely on that. Version ¶ src/pincfg_version.h defines HF_PINCFG_VERSION_MAJOR , _MINOR , _PATCH and HF_PINCFG_VERSION_STRING . A firmware version manifest can pick it up with __has_include("pincfg_version.h") . Next: Pin model .

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Select a board, include one header and read its pin map, in about a dozen lines. 1. Add the repository ¶ Most projects get it through hf-core-drivers as internal/hf-pincfg . On its own: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-pincfg.git external/hf-pincfg 2. Select the board ¶ Define exactly one board macro for every translation unit that includes the header, normally in the HAL's CMakeLists.txt : target_include_directories ( my_hal PUBLIC external/hf-pincfg/src ) target_compile_definitions ( my_hal PUBLIC HARDFOC_BOARD_VORTEX_V1=1 ) Without one, the selector stops the build with No supported board variant defined! . 3. Read the map ¶ tests/docs/quickstart.cpp #include "hf_functional_pin_config.hpp" // the build defines one HARDFOC_BOARD_* macro // Print where every pin that the GPIO layer should own lives on this board. void list_gpio_pins () { for ( size_t i = 0 ; i < HF_GPIO_MAPPING_SIZE ; ++ i ) { const HfGpioMapping & m = HF_GPIO_MAPPING [ i ]; if ( ! should_register_as_gpio ( static_cast < HfPinCategory > ( m . category ))) { continue ; // core and comm pins belong to the system and the bus drivers } std :: printf ( "%-28.*s chip %u pin %2u %s \n " , static_cast < int > ( m . name . size ()), m . name . data (), m . chip_type , m . physical_pin , m . is_inverted ? "active-low" : "active-high" ); } } What happens: Step What it does #include "hf_functional_pin_config.hpp" The selector includes the board header named by the define HF_GPIO_MAPPING , HF_GPIO_MAPPING_SIZE One HfGpioMapping per row of the board's GPIO list, in header order should_register_as_gpio() True for gpio and user rows; core and comm rows belong to the system and bus drivers m.chip_type , m.physical_pin Which chip carries the pin and its number on that chip The library needs C++20 ( std::string_view::starts_with ). If it does not compile ¶ Message Cause Fix No supported board variant defined! No HARDFOC_BOARD_* define reached this file Add it with PUBLIC scope, or to the component's compile options no member named 'starts_with' Built as C++17 Build with -std=c++20 or later redefinition of 'HfGpioChipType' Two board headers included Include only hf_functional_pin_config.hpp , never a board header directly Next: Integration .

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the headers and this site are checked on every pull request. Compile check ¶ tests/docs/quickstart.cpp holds every code block on this site. Compile it against each board before changing a header: for b in VORTEX_V1 FLUX_V1 ; do c++ -std = c++20 -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -Isrc -DHARDFOC_BOARD_ $b tests/docs/quickstart.cpp done Generated tables ¶ The pin maps and the board table are regions filled by tools/docs/generators/pins.py from the X-macro rows; the README example is copied from the compiled file by tools/docs/generators/snippets.py . hardfoc-docs check fails when a header changed and the page did not: pip install "git+https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-general-ci-tools@v1#subdirectory=packages/hardfoc-mkdocs-theme" hardfoc-docs gen # refresh after editing a header hardfoc-docs check # what CI runs mkdocs serve # preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000 CI workflows ¶ Workflow What it checks Docs Generated-table and figure drift, strict site build, Doxygen, offline link check, Lighthouse, screenshots; publishes on main and tags C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy on the headers C++ analysis cppcheck on src/ Markdown lint, YAML lint, link check Repository text files Release GitHub release on a v* tag The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of hf-general-ci-tools at @v1 .

docs.text: Vortex V1 pin map ¶ Every functional pin and ADC channel of the Vortex V1 motor controller board, generated from src/hf_functional_pin_config_vortex_v1.hpp . The MCU is an ESP32-C6. Besides its own GPIOs, the board routes control and status signals through a PCAL95555 I/O expander (I²C address 0x20 ) and two GPIOs of the TMC9660 motor controller. Select it with HARDFOC_BOARD_VORTEX_V1 . The board HAL is documented at hf-hal-vortex-v1 . GPIO ¶ Source: src/hf_functional_pin_config_vortex_v1.hpp , HF_FUNCTIONAL_GPIO_PIN_LIST (34 rows). Function Category Chip Pin Active Pull Drive Max (mA) XTAL_32K_P core MCU 0 high none push-pull 0 XTAL_32K_N core MCU 1 high none push-pull 0 BOOT_SEL core MCU 9 high none push-pull 0 JTAG_USB_D_N core MCU 12 high none push-pull 0 JTAG_USB_D_P core MCU 13 high none push-pull 0 SPI2_MISO comm MCU 2 high up push-pull 40 SPI2_SCK comm MCU 6 high none push-pull 40 SPI2_MOSI comm MCU 7 high none push-pull 40 SPI2_CS_TMC9660 comm MCU 18 low up push-pull 40 SPI2_CS_AS5047 comm MCU 20 low up push-pull 40 UART_RXD comm MCU 4 high up push-pull 40 UART_TXD comm MCU 5 high none push-pull 40 TWAI_TX comm MCU 14 high up push-pull 40 TWAI_RX comm MCU 15 high up push-pull 40 I2C_SDA comm MCU 21 high up push-pull 40 I2C_SCL comm MCU 22 high up push-pull 40 I2C_PCAL95555_INT comm MCU 23 low up push-pull 40 WS2812_LED_DAT comm MCU 3 high none push-pull 40 EXT_GPIO_CS_1 gpio MCU 19 low up push-pull 40 EXT_GPIO_CS_2 gpio MCU 8 low up push-pull 40 PCAL_TMC_FAULT_STATUS gpio PCAL95555 3 low none push-pull 25 PCAL_TMC_DRV_EN gpio PCAL95555 4 high none push-pull 25 PCAL_TMC_RST_CTRL gpio PCAL95555 5 high none push-pull 25 PCAL_PWR_GOOD gpio PCAL95555 6 high none push-pull 25 PCAL_CAN_HS_STB_OP gpio PCAL95555 10 high none push-pull 25 PCAL_IMU_BOOT gpio PCAL95555 11 low none push-pull 25 PCAL_IMU_INT gpio PCAL95555 12 low none push-pull 25 PCAL_IMU_RST gpio PCAL95555 15 low none push-pull 25 PCAL_TMC_SPI_COMM_EN gpio PCAL95555 13 low none push-pull 25 PCAL_TMC_WAKE_CTRL gpio PCAL95555 14 low none push-pull 25 PCAL_TMC_GPIO17_EXP_IN gpio PCAL95555 1 high none push-pull 25 PCAL_TMC_GPIO18_EXP_IN gpio PCAL95555 2 high none push-pull 25 TMC_GPIO17 gpio TMC9660 17 high none push-pull 25 TMC_GPIO18 gpio TMC9660 18 high none push-pull 25 Pin is the GPIO number on the MCU, the port bit (0 to 15) on the PCAL95555 and the GPIO number on the TMC9660. Active low means the row is PIN_LOGIC_INVERTED . One net, two rows TMC9660 GPIO17 and GPIO18 are wired to PCAL95555 inputs 1 and 2. PCAL_TMC_GPIO17_EXP_IN and PCAL_TMC_GPIO18_EXP_IN sample them at the expander; TMC_GPIO17 and TMC_GPIO18 configure and drive them inside the TMC9660. Both views see the same nets. Active low means the row is PIN_LOGIC_INVERTED . One net, two rows TMC9660 GPIO17 and GPIO18 are wired to PCAL95555 inputs 1 and 2. PCAL_TMC_GPIO17_EXP_IN and PCAL_TMC_GPIO18_EXP_IN sample them at the expander; TMC_GPIO17 and TMC_GPIO18 configure and drive them inside the TMC9660. Both views see the same nets.

docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs hardfoc-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. One row per pin, every table generated ¶ One row per pin, every table generated Figure description and sources From top to bottom. The HAL's build defines one HARDFOC_BOARD_* macro; the selector header (src/hf_functional_pin_config.hpp) includes that board's header. The board header holds two X-macro lists, one row per GPIO function and one per ADC channel. Expanding the lists produces the enums, name and category tables and the mapping arrays (names read from the Vortex V1 header). The board HAL's managers iterate the mapping arrays and look pins up by enum; no other code writes a pin number.
